statement.p: Decide whether (5,-2) and (-10,-7) are on the graph of the equation y=-\frac{3}{5}x+1\text{.}

solution.p: However if we substitute x=-10 and y=-7 into the equation, it leads to -7=7\text{,} which is false. This tells us that (-10,-7) is not on the graph.

########## # Solution ##########
BEGIN_PGML_SOLUTION If the point [`(5,-2)`] is on [`y=-\frac{3}{5}x+1\text{,}`] once we substitute [`x=5`] and [`y=-2`] into the line's equation, the equation should be true. Let's try:
[``` \begin{aligned} y\amp=-\frac{3}{5}x+1\\ -2\amp\wonder{=}-\frac{3}{5}(5)+1\\ -2\amp\confirm{=} -3+1 \end{aligned} ```]
Because this last equation is true, we can say that [`(5,-2)`] is on the graph of [`y=-\frac{3}{5}x+1\text{.}`]
However if we substitute [`x=-10`] and [`y=-7`] into the equation, it leads to [`-7=7\text{,}`] which is false. This tells us that [`(-10,-7)`] is _not_ on the graph.
